                    - script commands
                        
                        # 🐳 Core Dockerfile Commands
                        
                        ## 🔹 1. FROM
                        
                        ```
                        FROM node:18
                        ```
                        
                        👉 Base image
                        
                        👉 Starting point of your image
                        
                        ---
                        
                        ## 🔹 2. WORKDIR
                        
                        ```
                        WORKDIR /app
                        ```
                        
                        👉 Sets working directory inside container
                        
                        👉 Like `cd /app`
                        
                        ---
                        
                        ## 🔹 3. COPY
                        
                        ```
                        COPY . .
                        ```
                        
                        👉 Copies files from your machine → container
                        
                        ---
                        
                        ## 🔹 4. ADD
                        
                        ```
                        ADD file.zip .
                        ```
                        
                        👉 Same as COPY + extra features:
                        
                        - can extract archives
                        - can use URLs
                        
                        👉 ❗ rarely used (prefer COPY)
                        
                        ---
                        
                        ## 🔹 5. RUN
                        
                        ```
                        RUN npm install
                        ```
                        
                        👉 Runs command during **build time**
                        
                        👉 Creates new layer
                        
                        ---
                        
                        ## 🔹 6. CMD
                        
                        ```
                        CMD ["npm","start"]
                        ```
                        
                        👉 Default command when container starts
                        
                        👉 Can be overridden
                        
                        ---
                        
                        ## 🔹 7. ENTRYPOINT
                        
                        ```
                        ENTRYPOINT ["node","app.js"]
                        ```
                        
                        👉 Main fixed command
                        
                        👉 Harder to override
                        
                        ---
                        
                        ## 🔹 8. EXPOSE
                        
                        ```
                        EXPOSE3000
                        ```
                        
                        👉 Documents port
                        
                        👉 Does NOT actually open it
                        
                        ---
                        
                        ## 🔹 9. ENV
                        
                        ```
                        ENV NODE_ENV=production
                        ```
                        
                        👉 Sets environment variables
                        
                        ---
                        
                        ## 🔹 10. ARG
                        
                        ```
                        ARG VERSION=1.0
                        ```
                        
                        👉 Build-time variable (not available in container runtime)
                        
                        ---
                        
                        ## 🔹 11. VOLUME
                        
                        ```
                        VOLUME /data
                        ```
                        
                        👉 Creates mount point for persistent data
                        
                        ---
                        
                        ## 🔹 12. USER
                        
                        ```
                        USER node
                        ```
                        
                        👉 Runs container as non-root user (security)
                        
                        ---
                        
                        ## 🔹 13. LABEL
                        
                        ```
                        LABEL version="1.0"
                        ```
                        
                        👉 Metadata for image
                        
                        ---
                        
                        ## 🔹 14. HEALTHCHECK
                        
                        ```
                        HEALTHCHECK CMD curl -f http://localhost:3000 || exit 1
                        ```
                        
                        👉 Checks if container is healthy
                        
                        ---
                        
                        # 🧠 Build vs Run (VERY IMPORTANT)
                        
                        | Command | When it runs |
                        | --- | --- |
                        | RUN | build time |
                        | CMD | container start |
                        | ENTRYPOINT | container start |
                        
                        ---
                        
                        # 🔥 Minimal real example (your level)
                        
                        ```
                        FROM node:18
                        
                        WORKDIR /app
                        
                        COPY package.json .
                        RUN npm install
                        
                        COPY . .
                        
                        EXPOSE3000
                        
                        CMD ["npm","start"]
                        ```
                        
                        ---
                        
                        # ⚠️ Common mistakes
                        
                        ### ❌ Using RUN instead of CMD
                        
                        ```
                        RUN npm start  ❌
                        ```
                        
                        👉 runs during build, not container
                        
                        ---
                        
                        ### ❌ Thinking EXPOSE opens port
                        
                        ```
                        EXPOSE3000
                        ```
                        
                        👉 you still need:
                        
                        ```
                        -p3000:3000
                        ```
                        
                        ---
                        
                        # 🧠 Clean mental model
                        
                        ```
                        FROM → base
                        COPY → files
                        RUN → install/setup
                        CMD → run app
                        ```
                        
                        ---
                        
                        # 🔥 Interview answer
                        
                        > “Dockerfile instructions define how an image is built, where RUN executes commands at build time, while CMD and ENTRYPOINT define how the container runs.”
                        > 
                    - sample docker file
                        
                        ```jsx
                        # Base image
                        FROM node:18-alpine
                        
                        # Set working directory
                        WORKDIR /app
                        
                        # Copy dependency files first (for caching)
                        COPY package*.json ./
                        
                        # Install dependencies
                        RUN npm install
                        
                        # Copy rest of the project
                        COPY . .
                        
                        # Build project (for NestJS / TS)
                        RUN npm run build
                        
                        # Expose port
                        EXPOSE 3000
                        
                        # Run app
                        CMD ["node", "dist/main.js"]
                        ```
                        
                - 1. Debugging harder
                    
                    Docker debugging is harder because **the bug may be in 3 places, not 1**:
                    
                    ```
                    Your app ❌
                    Docker config ❌
                    Container environment ❌
                    ```
                    
                    ## When this happens
                    
                    Example: your NestJS app cannot connect to Postgres.
                    
                    Without Docker, you might use:
                    
                    ```
                    DB_HOST=localhost
                    ```
                    
                    Inside Docker, `localhost` means **inside the same container**, not your database container.
                    
                    So this fails:
                    
                    ```
                    DB_HOST=localhost
                    ```
                    
                    Correct:
                    
                    ```
                    DB_HOST=db
                    ```
                    
                    where `db` is the container/service name.
                    
                    ## Why it is harder
                    
                    Because Docker adds isolation:
                    
                    ```
                    App → Container filesystem
                    App → Container network
                    App → Container env variables
                    App → Docker volume
                    ```
                    
                    So the problem can be:
                    
                    ```
                    Wrong port
                    Wrong env
                    Wrong container name
                    Missing file inside image
                    Volume not mounted
                    Container exited
                    Docker cache used old code
                    ```
                    
                    ## How to solve/debug
                    
                    Use this order:
                    
                    ```
                    dockerps
                    ```
                    
                    Check if container is running.
                    
                    ```
                    docker logs container_name
                    ```
                    
                    See app error.
                    
                    ```
                    docker exec-it container_namesh
                    ```
                    
                    Enter container.
                    
                    ```
                    env
                    ```
                    
                    Check environment variables.
                    
                    ```
                    ls
                    ```
                    
                    Check whether files exist.
                    
                    ```
                    docker inspect container_name
                    ```
                    
                    Check ports, network, mounts.
                    
                    ## Most common fixes
                    
                    ```
                    docker build--no-cache-t my-app .
                    ```
                    
                    Fix old cache issue.
                    
                    ```
                    docker logs app
                    ```
                    
                    Read real crash reason.
                    
                    ```
                    docker exec-it appsh
                    ```
                    
                    Check inside container.
                    
                    ```
                    DB_HOST=db
                    ```
                    
                    Use service/container name, not `localhost`.
                    
                    ## Simple answer
                    
                    Docker debugging is harder because your app is running **inside an isolated mini-environment**, so you must debug both:
                    
                    ```
                    application logic + Docker environ
                    ```
                    
                - Container abstraction
                    
                    ## Container abstraction means
                    
                    Your app is **not running directly on your OS**.
                    
                    It runs inside an isolated box:
                    
                    ```
                    Your OS
                     └── Docker
                          └── Container
                               └── Your app
                    ```
                    
                    ## Why it causes problems
                    
                    Because inside the container:
                    
                    ```
                    localhost ≠ your computer
                    files ≠ your computer files
                    env variables may be different
                    ports are hidden unless mapped
                    installed packages may be different
                    ```
                    
                    So your app may work locally but fail in Docker.
                    
                    ## How to solve
                    
                    ### 1. Check logs
                    
                    ```
                    docker logs container_name
                    ```
                    
                    ### 2. Enter the container
                    
                    ```
                    docker exec-it container_namesh
                    ```
                    
                    ### 3. Check files
                    
                    ```
                    ls
                    pwd
                    ```
                    
                    ### 4. Check env variables
                    
                    ```
                    env
                    ```
                    
                    ### 5. Check ports
                    
                    ```
                    dockerps
                    ```
                    
                    Look at:
                    
                    ```
                    0.0.0.0:3000->3000/tcp
                    ```
                    
                    ### 6. Check network config
                    
                    ```
                    docker inspect container_name
                    ```
                    
                    ## Simple example
                    
                    Wrong inside Docker:
                    
                    ```
                    DATABASE_HOST=localhost
                    ```
                    
                    Correct when DB is another container:
                    
                    ```
                    DATABASE_HOST=postgres
                    ```
                    
                    ## Main idea
                    
                    Container abstraction makes debugging harder because you must ask:
                    
                    ```
                    Is the problem in my app?
                    Or inside the container environment?
                    ```
                    
                - 2. Networking complexity
                    
                    # 🧠 What “networking complexity” means
                    
                    > Your app is no longer talking directly to services — it talks through **Docker virtual network**
                    > 
                    
                    ---
                    
                    ## Without Docker
                    
                    ```
                    App → localhost:5432 (Postgres)
                    ```
                    
                    ---
                    
                    ## With Docker
                    
                    ```
                    App container → Docker network → DB container
                    ```
                    
                    👉 `localhost` is now **wrong**
                    
                    ---
                    
                    # ❌ Why it becomes complex
                    
                    Because Docker introduces:
                    
                    ### 1. Separate network per container
                    
                    Each container has its own:
                    
                    - IP
                    - network interface
                    
                    ---
                    
                    ### 2. Virtual DNS
                    
                    Containers talk by **name**, not IP
                    
                    ```
                    app → db:5432
                    ```
                    
                    ---
                    
                    ### 3. Port mapping layer
                    
                    ```
                    -p3000:3000
                    ```
                    
                    👉 Adds another layer:
                    
                    ```
                    Browser → host → container
                    ```
                    
                    ---
                    
                    # 🔥 When problems happen (real cases)
                    
                    ## ❌ Case 1 — Using localhost
                    
                    ```
                    DB_HOST=localhost
                    ```
                    
                    👉 Fails
                    
                    ✔ Fix:
                    
                    ```
                    DB_HOST=db
                    ```
                    
                    ---
                    
                    ## ❌ Case 2 — Wrong port
                    
                    ```
                    DB_PORT=5432
                    ```
                    
                    But container exposes:
                    
                    ```
                    -p5433:5432
                    ```
                    
                    👉 From host use `5433`
                    
                    👉 From container use `5432`
                    
                    ---
                    
                    ## ❌ Case 3 — Containers not in same network
                    
                    ```
                    docker run app
                    docker run db
                    ```
                    
                    👉 Cannot communicate ❌
                    
                    ✔ Fix:
                    
                    ```
                    docker network create mynet
                    
                    docker run--network mynet--name db postgres
                    docker run--network mynet--name app my-app
                    ```
                    
                    ---
                    
                    ## ❌ Case 4 — Service not ready
                    
                    App starts before DB
                    
                    👉 connection fails
                    
                    ✔ Fix:
                    
                    - retry logic
                    - wait-for script
                    
                    ---
                    
                    ## ❌ Case 5 — Port not exposed
                    
                    ```
                    EXPOSE3000
                    ```
                    
                    but forgot:
                    
                    ```
                    -p3000:3000
                    ```
                    
                    👉 Not accessible from outside
                    
                    ---
                    
                    # 🧠 How Docker networking actually works
                    
                    Docker creates:
                    
                    - bridge network (`docker0`)
                    - virtual interfaces (`veth`)
                    - NAT rules
                    
                    ---
                    
                    ## Flow:
                    
                    ```
                    Browser → Host port → Docker NAT → Container port
                    ```
                    
                    ---
                    
                    ## Internal communication:
                    
                    ```
                    app → db (via Docker DNS)
                    ```
                    
                    ---
                    
                    # 🛠 How to debug networking
                    
                    ### 1. Check containers
                    
                    ```
                    dockerps
                    ```
                    
                    ---
                    
                    ### 2. Check network
                    
                    ```
                    docker networkls
                    docker network inspect mynet
                    ```
                    
                    ---
                    
                    ### 3. Enter container
                    
                    ```
                    docker exec-it appsh
                    ```
                    
                    ---
                    
                    ### 4. Test connection
                    
                    ```
                    ping db
                    ```
                    
                    or:
                    
                    ```
                    nc-zv db5432
                    ```
                    
                    ---
                    
                    ### 5. Check ports
                    
                    ```
                    dockerps
                    ```
                    
                    Look for:
                    
                    ```
                    0.0.0.0:3000->3000
                    ```
                    
                    ---
                    
                    # 🧠 Golden rules (remember these)
                    
                    ### Rule 1
                    
                    ```
                    localhost = same container only
                    ```
                    
                    ---
                    
                    ### Rule 2
                    
                    ```
                    Container → container = use service name
                    ```
                    
                    ---
                    
                    ### Rule 3
                    
                    ```
                    Host → container = use mapped port
                    ```
                    
                    ---
                    
                    # 🔥 Simple example (your level)
                    
                    ### Setup:
                    
                    ```
                    backend → NestJS
                    db → Postgres
                    ```
                    
                    ---
                    
                    ### Correct config:
                    
                    ```
                    DB_HOST=db
                    DB_PORT=5432
                    ```
                    
                    ---
                    
                    # 🧠 Interview answer
                    
                    > “Docker networking is complex because containers run in isolated networks, so communication requires proper service naming, port mapping, and shared networks instead of relying on localhost.”
                    > 
                - 3. Data persistence
                    
                    ## Data persistence issue in Docker
                    
                    By default, container data is **temporary**.
                    
                    A container has its own writable layer:
                    
                    ```
                    image layers  +  container writable layer
                    ```
                    
                    When the container is removed, that writable layer is removed too.
                    
                    So if Postgres saves data inside the container and you delete/recreate the container:
                    
                    ```
                    dockerrm db
                    ```
                    
                    your database data can be gone.
                    
                    ## Where this happens
                    
                    Mostly with stateful services:
                    
                    ```
                    Postgres
                    MySQL
                    MongoDB
                    Redis
                    uploaded files
                    logs
                    generated reports
                    ```
                    
                    Example:
                    
                    ```
                    docker run--name db postgres
                    ```
                    
                    Postgres stores data inside container filesystem. Bad for real apps.
                    
                    ## How to solve
                    
                    Use a **volume**.
                    
                    ```
                    docker volume create pgdata
                    ```
                    
                    Run Postgres with volume:
                    
                    ```
                    docker run \
                    --name db \
                    -ePOSTGRES_PASSWORD=password \
                    -v pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data \
                      postgres
                    ```
                    
                    Now data is stored in Docker volume, not only inside the container.
                    
                    Container can be removed/recreated, but volume remains.
                    
                    ## In Docker Compose
                    
                    ```
                    services:
                      db:
                        image: postgres
                        environment:
                          POSTGRES_PASSWORD: password
                        volumes:
                          - pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data
                    
                    volumes:
                      pgdata:
                    ```
                    
                    ## Simple rule
                    
                    ```
                    Container = temporary
                    Volume = persistent
                    ```
                    
                    So for databases, always use volumes.
                    
            - single vs Multi Stage builds
                
                # 🧠 Single-stage vs Multi-stage builds
                
                ## 🔹 1. Single-stage build
                
                👉 Everything happens in **one image**
                
                ```
                FROM node:18
                
                WORKDIR /app
                
                COPY . .
                
                RUN npm install
                RUN npm run build
                
                CMD ["node","dist/main.js"]
                ```
                
                ---
                
                ## ❌ Problem
                
                This image contains:
                
                ```
                node_modules (dev deps)
                build tools
                source code
                unnecessary files
                ```
                
                👉 Result:
                
                - ❌ large image
                - ❌ slower deploy
                - ❌ less secure
                
                ---
                
                # 🔹 2. Multi-stage build
                
                👉 Use **multiple stages**, but final image is clean
                
                ---
                
                ## ✅ Example
                
                ```
                # Stage 1 — build
                FROM node:18AS builder
                
                WORKDIR /app
                
                COPY package*.json ./
                RUN npm install
                
                COPY . .
                RUN npm run build
                
                # Stage 2 — production
                FROM node:18-alpine
                
                WORKDIR /app
                
                COPY package*.json ./
                RUN npm install --omit=dev
                
                COPY --from=builder /app/dist ./dist
                
                EXPOSE3000
                
                CMD ["node","dist/main.js"]
                ```
                
                ---
                
                # 🔥 What happens
                
                ```
                Stage 1 → build everything
                Stage 2 → take ONLY needed files
                ```
                
                ---
                
                ## 🧠 Final image contains ONLY:
                
                ```
                dist/
                production node_modules
                minimal runtime
                ```
                
                ---
                
                # ⚡ Key differences
                
                | Feature | Single-stage | Multi-stage |
                | --- | --- | --- |
                | Image size | big ❌ | small ✅ |
                | Security | low ❌ | higher ✅ |
                | Build tools inside | yes ❌ | no ✅ |
                | Production ready | not ideal ❌ | best practice ✅ |
                
                ---
                
                # 🧠 Why multi-stage is powerful
                
                👉 You separate:
                
                ```
                build environment ≠ runtime environment
                ```
                
                ---
                
                # 🔥 Real-world impact
                
                Without multi-stage:
                
                ```
                Image size: 800MB ❌
                ```
                
                With multi-stage:
                
                ```
                Image size: 150MB ✅
                ```
                
                ---
                
                # ⚠️ Interview trap
                
                > “Does multi-stage create multiple containers?”
                > 
                
                👉 ❌ NO
                
                👉 It creates **one final image only**
                
                ---
                
                # 🧠 Clean mental model
                
                ```
                Stage 1 → build
                Stage 2 → clean runtime
                Final → only last stage used
                ```
                
                ---
                
                # 🔥 Interview answer
                
                > “Single-stage builds include everything in one image, while multi-stage builds separate build and runtime environments, resulting in smaller, more secure production images.”
                > 
            - QA

                > 
                > 
                > # 🐳 Docker Q&A (100)
                > 
                > ---
                > 
                > ### 1. What is Docker?
                > 
                > Docker is a containerization platform.
                > 
                > It packages apps with dependencies.
                > 
                > Runs consistently across environments.
                > 
                > ---
                > 
                > ### 2. What is a container?
                > 
                > A container is a running instance of an image.
                > 
                > It is an isolated process.
                > 
                > Uses OS-level virtualization.
                > 
                > ---
                > 
                > ### 3. What is a Docker image?
                > 
                > An image is a read-only template.
                > 
                > It contains app + dependencies.
                > 
                > Used to create containers.
                > 
                > ---
                > 
                > ### 4. Difference between image and container?
                > 
                > Image = static blueprint.
                > 
                > Container = running instance.
                > 
                > One image → many containers.
                > 
                > ---
                > 
                > ### 5. What is Dockerfile?
                > 
                > It is a script to build images.
                > 
                > Contains instructions like FROM, COPY.
                > 
                > Defines how image is created.
                > 
                > ---
                > 
                > ### 6. What does FROM do?
                > 
                > Defines base image.
                > 
                > Starting point of build.
                > 
                > Example: node:18.
                > 
                > ---
                > 
                > ### 7. What does WORKDIR do?
                > 
                > Sets working directory inside container.
                > 
                > Like `cd` command.
                > 
                > Used for all next instructions.
                > 
                > ---
                > 
                > ### 8. What does COPY do?
                > 
                > Copies files into container.
                > 
                > From host → container.
                > 
                > Used for app code.
                > 
                > ---
                > 
                > ### 9. What does RUN do?
                > 
                > Executes commands at build time.
                > 
                > Creates new image layer.
                > 
                > Used for installs.
                > 
                > ---
                > 
                > ### 10. What does CMD do?
                > 
                > Defines default runtime command.
                > 
                > Runs when container starts.
                > 
                > Can be overridden.
                > 
                > ---
                > 
                > ### 11. What is ENTRYPOINT?
                > 
                > Defines fixed command.
                > 
                > Harder to override than CMD.
                > 
                > Used for main executable.
                > 
                > ---
                > 
                > ### 12. What is EXPOSE?
                > 
                > Documents port usage.
                > 
                > Does not open port.
                > 
                > Used for clarity.
                > 
                > ---
                > 
                > ### 13. What is ENV?
                > 
                > Defines environment variables.
                > 
                > Used at runtime.
                > 
                > Example: NODE_ENV.
                > 
                > ---
                > 
                > ### 14. What is ARG?
                > 
                > Build-time variable.
                > 
                > Not available at runtime.
                > 
                > Used during build only.
                > 
                > ---
                > 
                > ### 15. What is VOLUME?
                > 
                > Defines persistent storage path.
                > 
                > Data survives container deletion.
                > 
                > Used for DB.
                > 
                > ---
                > 
                > ### 16. What is Docker Compose?
                > 
                > Tool for multi-container apps.
                > 
                > Uses YAML config.
                > 
                > Runs multiple services together.
                > 
                > ---
                > 
                > ### 17. What does `docker build` do?
                > 
                > Builds image from Dockerfile.
                > 
                > Uses instructions step-by-step.
                > 
                > Creates layers.
                > 
                > ---
                > 
                > ### 18. What does `docker run` do?
                > 
                > Creates and starts container.
                > 
                > From image.
                > 
                > Runs app.
                > 
                > ---
                > 
                > ### 19. What does `docker ps` do?
                > 
                > Lists running containers.
                > 
                > Shows IDs and ports.
                > 
                > Used for monitoring.
                > 
                > ---
                > 
                > ### 20. What is `docker exec`?
                > 
                > Runs command inside container.
                > 
                > Used for debugging.
                > 
                > Example: shell access.
                > 
                > ---
                > 
                > ### 21. What is `docker logs`?
                > 
                > Shows container output.
                > 
                > Reads stdout/stderr.
                > 
                > Used for debugging.
                > 
                > ---
                > 
                > ### 22. What is a layer?
                > 
                > Each Dockerfile step creates layer.
                > 
                > Layers are cached.
                > 
                > Used for efficiency.
                > 
                > ---
                > 
                > ### 23. What is caching in Docker?
                > 
                > Reuses unchanged layers.
                > 
                > Speeds up build.
                > 
                > Depends on file changes.
                > 
                > ---
                > 
                > ### 24. What is `.dockerignore`?
                > 
                > Excludes files from build.
                > 
                > Improves performance.
                > 
                > Like `.gitignore`.
                > 
                > ---
                > 
                > ### 25. What is a volume?
                > 
                > Persistent storage.
                > 
                > Stored outside container.
                > 
                > Used for databases.
                > 
                > ---
                > 
                > ### 26. What is bind mount?
                > 
                > Maps local folder to container.
                > 
                > Direct file sharing.
                > 
                > Used in development.
                > 
                > ---
                > 
                > ### 27. What is Docker network?
                > 
                > Virtual network for containers.
                > 
                > Allows communication.
                > 
                > Provides DNS.
                > 
                > ---
                > 
                > ### 28. What is bridge network?
                > 
                > Default Docker network.
                > 
                > Containers get IPs.
                > 
                > Used locally.
                > 
                > ---
                > 
                > ### 29. What is host network?
                > 
                > Shares host network.
                > 
                > No isolation.
                > 
                > Faster but risky.
                > 
                > ---
                > 
                > ### 30. What is overlay network?
                > 
                > Used in Docker Swarm.
                > 
                > Multi-host networking.
                > 
                > For distributed systems.
                > 
                > ---
                > 
                > ### 31. Why use Docker?
                > 
                > Consistency across environments.
                > 
                > Easy deployment.
                > 
                > Isolation of apps.
                > 
                > ---
                > 
                > ### 32. Docker vs VM?
                > 
                > Docker shares kernel.
                > 
                > VM has full OS.
                > 
                > Docker is lighter.
                > 
                > ---
                > 
                > ### 33. What is container isolation?
                > 
                > Isolation via namespaces.
                > 
                > Separate processes/network.
                > 
                > Secure execution.
                > 
                > ---
                > 
                > ### 34. What are namespaces?
                > 
                > Kernel feature.
                > 
                > Isolates processes.
                > 
                > Used in containers.
                > 
                > ---
                > 
                > ### 35. What are cgroups?
                > 
                > Resource limits system.
                > 
                > Controls CPU, RAM.
                > 
                > Prevents overuse.
                > 
                > ---
                > 
                > ### 36. What is Docker daemon?
                > 
                > Background service.
                > 
                > Manages containers/images.
                > 
                > Called `dockerd`.
                > 
                > ---
                > 
                > ### 37. What is containerd?
                > 
                > Container runtime manager.
                > 
                > Handles lifecycle.
                > 
                > Used by Docker.
                > 
                > ---
                > 
                > ### 38. What is runc?
                > 
                > Low-level runtime.
                > 
                > Creates containers.
                > 
                > Uses kernel features.
                > 
                > ---
                > 
                > ### 39. What is Docker Hub?
                > 
                > Public image registry.
                > 
                > Stores images.
                > 
                > Used to pull/push.
                > 
                > ---
                > 
                > ### 40. What is tagging?
                > 
                > Naming images with versions.
                > 
                > Example: node:18.
                > 
                > Used for version control.
                > 
                > ---
                > 
                > ### 41. What is multi-stage build?
                > 
                > Multiple build phases.
                > 
                > Final image is clean.
                > 
                > Reduces size.
                > 
                > ---
                > 
                > ### 42. Why multi-stage?
                > 
                > Smaller images.
                > 
                > Better security.
                > 
                > No build tools inside.
                > 
                > ---
                > 
                > ### 43. What is image size optimization?
                > 
                > Using alpine images.
                > 
                > Removing unnecessary files.
                > 
                > Multi-stage builds.
                > 
                > ---
                > 
                > ### 44. What is container lifecycle?
                > 
                > Created → running → stopped → removed.
                > 
                > States of container.
                > 
                > Managed by Docker.
                > 
                > ---
                > 
                > ### 45. What is ephemeral container?
                > 
                > Temporary container.
                > 
                > Data lost on delete.
                > 
                > Default behavior.
                > 
                > ---
                > 
                > ### 46. Why debugging Docker is hard?
                > 
                > Extra abstraction layer.
                > 
                > Isolation hides issues.
                > 
                > Multiple failure points.
                > 
                > ---
                > 
                > ### 47. What is port mapping?
                > 
                > Maps host → container port.
                > 
                > Example: -p 3000:3000.
                > 
                > Required for access.
                > 
                > ---
                > 
                > ### 48. What is service discovery?
                > 
                > Finding containers by name.
                > 
                > Docker DNS handles it.
                > 
                > Used in Compose.
                > 
                > ---
                > 
                > ### 49. What is `depends_on`?
                > 
                > Defines dependency order.
                > 
                > Starts services first.
                > 
                > Does NOT wait for readiness.
                > 
                > ---
                > 
                > ### 50. Why `localhost` fails in Docker?
                > 
                > Points to same container.
                > 
                > Not other services.
                > 
                > Use service name instead.
                > 
                > ---
                > 
                > (Continuing...)
                > 
                > ---
                > 
                > ### 51–100 (condensed but same style)
                > 
                > 1. What is Docker Compose file?
                > YAML config for services.
                > Defines containers.
                > Used to run system.
                > 
                > ---
                > 
                > 1. What is build context?
                > Folder sent to Docker.
                > Used in build.
                > Defined in build:.
                > 
                > ---
                > 
                > 1. What is image immutability?
                > Images cannot change.
                > New version → new image.
                > Ensures consistency.
                > 
                > ---
                > 
                > 1. What is container restart?
                > Restart policy.
                > Used for recovery.
                > Example: always.
                > 
                > ---
                > 
                > 1. What is healthcheck?
                > Checks container health.
                > Used for monitoring.
                > Defined in Dockerfile.
                > 
                > ---
                > 
                > 1. What is docker system prune?
                > Removes unused data.
                > Frees space.
                > Deletes unused containers.
                > 
                > ---
                > 
                > 1. What is docker inspect?
                > Shows container details.
                > JSON output.
                > Used for debugging.
                > 
                > ---
                > 
                > 1. What is docker-compose up?
                > Starts all services.
                > Builds if needed.
                > Runs containers.
                > 
                > ---
                > 
                > 1. What is docker-compose down?
                > Stops and removes containers.
                > Deletes network.
                > Used to clean.
                > 
                > ---
                > 
                > 1. What is docker-compose logs?
                > Shows logs of services.
                > Used for debugging.
                > Supports filtering.
            - DOCKER COMPOSE
                
                # 🧩 What is Docker Compose
                
                > Tool to **run multiple containers together** using one file
                > 
                
                ---
                
                # 🧠 Problem it solves
                
                Without Compose:
                
                ```
                docker run app
                docker run db
                docker run redis
                ```
                
                👉 Hard to manage ❌
                
                ---
                
                # ✅ With Compose
                
                ```
                services:
                  app:
                  db:
                  redis:
                ```
                
                👉 One command runs everything
                
                ---
                
                # ⚙️ How it works
                
                ```
                docker-compose.yml → defines services
                docker compose up → creates containers
                docker network → connects them
                ```
                
                ---
                
                # 🔥 What is a “service”
                
                ```
                app:
                  build: .
                ```
                
                👉 Service = **one container config**
                
                ---
                
                # 🧠 What Compose does internally
                
                ```
                1. Builds images (if needed)
                2. Creates containers
                3. Creates network
                4. Connects containers
                5. Starts everything
                ```
                
                ---
                
                # 🔗 Communication
                
                ```
                app → db
                ```
                
                👉 uses service name as hostname
                
                ---
                
                # 📦 Example
                
                ```
                services:
                  app:
                    build: .
                  db:
                    image: postgres
                ```
                
                👉 Runs:
                
                ```
                Container 1 → app
                Container 2 → db
                ```
                
                ---
                
                # ⚠️ Important rules
                
                ```
                1 service = 1 container
                NOT multiple containers
                ```
                
                ---
                
                # 🧠 Final mental model
                
                ```
                Dockerfile → build ONE app
                Compose → run WHOLE system
                ```
                
                ---
                
                # 🔥 One-line interview answer
                
                > “Docker Compose is used to define and run multi-container applications using a single YAML configuration file.”
                > 
        - Cookie
            
            # 🍪 Cookie — Deep Dive (Backend-focused)
            
            ---
            
            # 🧠 What is a Cookie?
            
            A **cookie** is:
            
            ```
            Small key-value data stored in the browser and automatically sent with every request to the server.
            ```
            
            Example:
            
            ```
            Set-Cookie: sessionId=abc123
            ```
            
            Browser stores it, then sends:
            
            ```
            Cookie: sessionId=abc123
            ```
            
            ---
            
            # ⚙️ Why cookies exist (REAL reason)
            
            Originally created to:
            
            ```
            Maintain state in HTTP (which is stateless)
            ```
            
            👉 HTTP does NOT remember users between requests.
            
            So cookies allow:
            
            ```
            Server: “I remember you”
            ```
            
            ---
            
            # 🧩 What data is stored in cookie?
            
            ```
            name=value
            ```
            
            Example:
            
            ```
            refreshToken=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9...
            ```
            
            Plus metadata (very important):
            
            - expires / maxAge
            - domain
            - path
            - secure
            - httpOnly
            - sameSite
            
            ---
            
            # 🔁 How cookies work (under the hood)
            
            ---
            
            ## Step 1 — Server sets cookie
            
            ```
            res.cookie("refreshToken",token, {
              httpOnly:true
            });
            ```
            
            ---
            
            ## Step 2 — Browser stores cookie
            
            Internally in browser storage
            
            ---
            
            ## Step 3 — Browser sends automatically
            
            ```
            Cookie: refreshToken=...
            ```
            
            👉 You DO NOT manually add it
            
            ---
            
            # 🧠 Why cookies are used
            
            ---
            
            ## 1. Maintain login sessions
            
            ```
            sessionId → identify user
            ```
            
            ---
            
            ## 2. Store refresh tokens
            
            ```
            Long-lived authentication token
            ```
            
            ---
            
            ## 3. Store user preferences
            
            ```
            theme=dark
            language=en
            ```
            
            ---
            
            # 🔥 Why backend uses cookies (IMPORTANT)
            
            ---
            
            ## Key advantage:
            
            ```
            Browser automatically sends cookie
            ```
            
            So backend does NOT need frontend to attach anything.
            
            ---
            
            ## Especially for refresh token
            
            Because:
            
            ```
            Refresh requests should be automatic and secure
            ```
            
            ---
            
            # ⚔️ Cookie vs localStorage vs sessionStorage
            
            ---
            
            ## 🔹 localStorage
            
            ```
            Persistent storage in browser (no expiration)
            ```
            
            Example:
            
            ```
            localStorage.setItem("token","abc");
            ```
            
            ### Properties:
            
            - persists after tab close
            - accessible via JS
            - NOT sent automatically
            
            ---
            
            ## 🔹 sessionStorage
            
            ```
            Storage limited to one tab session
            ```
            
            - cleared when tab closes
            - accessible via JS
            - NOT sent automatically
            
            ---
            
            ## 🔹 Cookie
            
            ```
            Automatic browser storage tied to domain
            ```
            
            - can expire
            - automatically sent
            - can be hidden from JS (httpOnly)
            
            ---
            
            # ⚔️ Comparison table
            
            | Feature | Cookie | localStorage | sessionStorage |
            | --- | --- | --- | --- |
            | Sent automatically | ✅ Yes | ❌ No | ❌ No |
            | Accessible by JS | Optional | ✅ Yes | ✅ Yes |
            | Expiration | Yes | No | On tab close |
            | Security (XSS) | HIGH (httpOnly) | LOW | LOW |
            | CSRF risk | HIGH | NONE | NONE |
            
            ---
            
            # 🔐 Cookie security attributes (CRITICAL)
            
            ---
            
            ## 🔹 httpOnly
            
            ```
            JS cannot read cookie
            ```
            
            👉 protects against XSS
            
            ---
            
            ## 🔹 secure
            
            ```
            Only sent over HTTPS
            ```
            
            ---
            
            ## 🔹 sameSite
            
            Controls cross-site behavior
            
            ### Values:
            
            ```
            strict → only same site
            lax → limited cross-site
            none → full cross-site (needs HTTPS)
            ```
            
            ---
            
            # 🔥 Why backend stores refresh token in cookie
            
            ---
            
            ## Problem
            
            If you store refresh token in localStorage:
            
            ```
            XSS → attacker steals it
            ```
            
            ---
            
            ## Solution
            
            Store in cookie:
            
            ```
            res.cookie("refreshToken",token, {
              httpOnly:true,
              secure:true,
              sameSite:"strict"
            });
            ```
            
            ---
            
            ## Why this is good
            
            ```
            JS cannot access token → safer
            Browser sends it automatically → easier
            ```
            
            ---
            
            # ⚠️ Is it OK to store refresh token in cookie?
            
            👉 YES — this is **industry standard**
            
            BUT ONLY if:
            
            ---
            
            ## ✅ You configure correctly
            
            ```
            res.cookie("refreshToken",token, {
              httpOnly:true,
              secure:true,
              sameSite:"lax"// or strict depending
            });
            ```
            
            ---
            
            ## ❗ AND handle CSRF
            
            Because:
            
            ```
            Cookies are automatically sent → CSRF possible
            ```
            
            So you must:
            
            - use SameSite
            - validate origin
            - optionally use CSRF token
            
            ---
            
            # 🧠 Best modern pattern (IMPORTANT)
            
            ---
            
            ## Hybrid auth
            
            ```
            Access token → header
            Refresh token → cookie
            ```
            
            ---
            
            ## Why?
            
            ### Access token:
            
            ```
            Short-lived → low risk
            Manual control → no CSRF
            ```
            
            ---
            
            ### Refresh token:
            
            ```
            Long-lived → needs protection
            Stored in httpOnly cookie → safe from XSS
            ```
            
            ---
            
            # ⚠️ Common mistakes
            
            ---
            
            ## ❌ Store refresh token in localStorage
            
            → XSS vulnerability
            
            ---
            
            ## ❌ Cookie without httpOnly
            
            → JS can steal it
            
            ---
            
            ## ❌ Cookie without sameSite
            
            → CSRF risk
            
            ---
            
            ## ❌ Using  CORS with credentials
            
            → security issue
            
            ---
            
            # 🧠 Senior-level insight
            
            👉 Cookies are NOT “old”
            
            They are:
            
            ```
            A secure transport layer for sensitive data
            ```
            
            Used correctly:
            
            ```
            They are MORE secure than localStorage
            ```
            
            ---
            
            # 🧭 Final mental model
            
            ```
            Cookie → automatic, secure transport
            localStorage → manual, flexible but risky
            sessionStorage → temporary per-tab storage
            ```
            
            ---
            
            # 🔥 Final answer to your question
            
            👉 Yes:
            
            ```
            It is correct and recommended to store refresh token in httpOnly cookie
            ```
            
            But only with:
            
            ```
            httpOnly + secure + sameSite + CSRF protection
            ```
