- JAVASCRIPT
    - DEFINITION
        
        > 
        > 
    - **Map (and Set) vs key-value_data**
        - ALL
            - MAP
                
                > A Map is a collection of key-value pairs where keys can be **any type** (object, function, primitive).
                > 
            - SET
                
                > A Set is a collection of **unique values** (no duplicates allowed).
                > 
            - key-value
                
                > A key-value pair is a data structure where each key is associated with a value.
                > 
            - MAP
                
                > A key-value pair is a data structure where each key is associated with a value.
                > 
                - USAGE
                    - getting value
                        
                        ```jsx
                        map.get("name"); // "John"
                        ```
                        
                    - checking the key
                        
                        ```jsx
                        map.has("name"); // true
                        ```
                        
                    - deleting
                        
                        ```jsx
                        map.delete("name");
                        ```
                        
                    - size
                        
                        ```jsx
                        map.size;
                        ```
                        
                    - iteration
                        
                        ```jsx
                        for (let [key, value] of map) {
                          console.log(key, value);
                        }
                        ```
                        
                    
                    ```jsx
                    const map = new Map()
                    map.set("name", "John");
                    map.set(1, "number key");
                    map.set(true, "boolean key");
                    map.set({}, "object key");
                    ```
                    
            - SET
                - USAGE
                    - Creating
                        
                        ```jsx
                        const set = new Set();
                        ```
                        
                    - Adding
                        
                        ```jsx
                        set.add(1);
                        set.add(2);
                        set.add(2); // ignored
                        ```
                        
                    - checking
                        
                        ```jsx
                        set.has(1); // true
                        ```
                        
                    - deleting
                        
                        ```jsx
                        set.delete(1);
                        ```
                        
                    - size
                        
                        ```jsx
                        set.size;
                        ```
                        
                    - iteration
                        
                        ```jsx
                        for (let value of set) {
                          console.log(value);
                        }
                        ```
                        
                    - OBJECT limitation vs MAP
                        
                        > 
                        > 
                        > 
                        > Objects:
                        > 
                        > - keys are converted to strings
                        > 
                        > Map:
                        > 
                        > - preserves original key type
                        > - Map is designed for performance and frequent updates, Object is designed for simplicity and JSON-like data.
                        
                        ```jsx
                        const obj = {};
                        obj[1] = "number";
                        obj["1"] = "string";
                        
                        console.log(obj); // { "1": "string" }
                        ```
                        
            - MAP vs OBJECT vs SET
                
                > 
                > 
                > 
                > 
                > | Feature | Object | Map | Set |
                > | --- | --- | --- | --- |
                > | Structure | Key-value | Key-value | Unique values |
                > | Key types | string/symbol | any type | values only |
                > | Order | partial | guaranteed | guaranteed |
                > | Duplicates | allowed in values | allowed | ❌ not allowed |
                > | Size tracking | manual | `.size` | `.size` |
                > | Performance | general | better for frequent ops | fast uniqueness checks |
            - WHEN TO USE WHICH
                
                > 
                > 
                > 
                > ## 🟡 Use Object when:
                > 
                > - simple data structure
                > - static configuration
                > - JSON-like data
                > 
                > ---
                > 
                > ## 🟢 Use Map when:
                > 
                > - frequent insert/delete operations
                > - dynamic keys
                > - caching system
                > - session storage
                > - backend-like logic
                > 
                > ---
                > 
                > ## 🔵 Use Set when:
                > 
                > - removing duplicates
                > - tracking unique items
                > - checking existence fast
            - Real-world usage
                - MAP
                    
                    ```jsx
                    🗂️ Map in backend:
                    in-memory cache
                    request tracking
                    session storage
                    rate limiting
                    const cache = new Map();
                    
                    function getUser(id) {
                      if (cache.has(id)) return cache.get(id);
                    
                      const user = fetchFromDB(id);
                      cache.set(id, user);
                    
                      return user;
                    }
                    ```
                    
                - SET
                    
                    ```jsx
                    🔵 Set in backend:
                    unique active users
                    duplicate prevention
                    tracking connected clients
                    const activeUsers = new Set();
                    
                    activeUsers.add("user1");
                    activeUsers.add("user1"); // ignored
                    ```
                    
            - MENTAL MODEL
                
                > 
                > 
                > 
                > ## Map
                > 
                > > Fast dictionary for storing relationships
                > > 
                > 
                > ## 🔵 Set
                > 
                > > Fast filter for uniqueness
                > > 
                > 
                > ## 🗂️ Object
                > 
                > > Simple static structure (JSON-like)
                > >

            > **V8 is a JavaScript engine that executes JS code by compiling it into machine code (not interpreting it directly).**
            > 
            > Used in:
            > 
            > - Google Chrome
            > - Node.js
            > - Edge (Chromium)
        - Ignition Interpreter
            
            > 
            > 
            > 
            > # Ignition Interpreter
            > 
            > Ignition:
            > 
            > - Walks the AST
            > - Emits bytecode
            > - Executes it
            > 
            > ---
            > 
            > ## 🧠 Internals (Important)
            > 
            > Ignition uses:
            > 
            > ### ▶️ Register Machine (NOT stack-based)
            > 
            > Unlike some engines:
            > 
            > - Uses **registers** (`r0`, `r1`, …)
            > - More efficient than stack machines
            > 
            > ---
            > 
            > ## Example
            > 
            > ```
            > letx=10+20;
            > ```
            > 
            > ---
            > 
            > ### Bytecode (conceptual)
            > 
            > ```
            > LdaSmi 10     ; load small integer 10
            > AddSmi 20     ; add 20
            > Star r0       ; store in register r0 (x)
            > ```
            > 
            > ---
            > 
            > ## 💡 Instruction Meaning
            > 
            > | Instruction | Meaning |
            > | --- | --- |
            > | `LdaSmi` | Load small integer |
            > | `AddSmi` | Add small integer |
            > | `Star` | Store in register |
        - FLOW
            
            > 
            > 
            > 
            > ![image.png](DOCUMENTATIONS/image%2065.png)
            > 
        - HIGH LEVEL ARCHITECTURE
            
            > 
            > 
            > 
            > JavaScript Code
            > ↓
            > Parser
            > ↓
            > AST (Abstract Syntax Tree)
            > ↓
            > Ignition (Interpreter)
            > ↓
            > TurboFan (JIT Compiler)
            > ↓
            > Machine Code (CPU executes)
            > 
        - ENGINEs
            
            > The JavaScript engine executes and compiles JavaScript into native machine code. Every major browser has developed its own JS engine: Google's Chrome uses V8, Safari uses JavaScriptCore, and Firefox  uses  SpiderMonkey.
            > 
        - LIFECYCLE
            
            > 
            > 
            > 
            > # 🧠 FINAL FLOW (ONE LINE VIEW)
            > 
            > ```
            > JS Code
            >   ↓
            > Tokenizer
            >   ↓
            > Parser → AST
            >   ↓
            > Ignition (Bytecode)
            >   ↓
            > Interpreter Execution
            >   ↓
            > Profiler (Hot Code Detection)
            >   ↓
            > TurboFan (Optimization)
            >   ↓
            > Optimized Machine Code
            >   ↓
            > (Deopt if needed)
            >   ↓
            > Garbage Collection (parallel)
            > ```
            > 
            
            > 
            > 
            > 
            > # ⚡ AST → Bytecode (Ignition Deep Dive)
            > 
            > Inside the V8 JavaScript Engine, this step converts your AST into **bytecode** using:
            > 
            > 👉 **Ignition (Interpreter)**
            > 
            > ---
            > 
            > # 🚀 High-Level Flow
            > 
            > ```
            > AST → Bytecode → Execution (Interpreter)
            > ```
            > 
            > ---
            > 
            > # 🧠 1. What is Bytecode?
            > 
            > 👉 Bytecode = **low-level instructions for a virtual machine**
            > 
            > - Not machine code ❌
            > - Not high-level JS ❌
            > - Middle layer ✅
            > 
            > Think:
            > 
            > ```
            > JS → (AST) → Bytecode → (later) Machine Code
            > ```
            > 
            > ---
            > 
            > ## 🔥 Why Bytecode exists?
            > 
            > Directly compiling JS → machine code is slow because:
            > 
            > - JS is dynamic (types change)
            > - Needs runtime feedback
            > 
            > 👉 So V8 uses:
            > 
            > 1. **Fast start (bytecode)**
            > 2. **Then optimize later (TurboFan)**
        - DETAILED_LIFECYCLE
            - DEFINITION
                
                > The first thing V8 does is parse your raw JavaScript source code. It doesn't execute anything yet. The goal is to turn your string of characters into a structured representation the machine can understand. This process involves two key components:
                > 
            - Parsing
                
                > The [parser](https://github.com/v8/v8/blob/master/src/parsing/parser.h) picks it up and creates an [Abstract Syntax Tree (AST)](https://github.com/v8/v8/tree/master/src/ast): a tree representation of the source code. Each node of the tree denotes a construct occurring in the code.
                > 
                - Parsing steps
                    - Raw javascript input
                        
                        > 
                        > 
                        > 
                        > Example:
                        > 
                        > ```
                        > letresult=10+20;
                        > ```
                        > 
                        > At this point:
                        > 
                        > 👉 It’s just a string in memory
                        > 
                        > 👉 No meaning yet for the engine
                        > 
                    - Lexical Analysis (Tokenizer / Scanner)
                        
                        > 
                        > 
                        > 
                        > ## What it does
                        > 
                        > Breaks code into **tokens** (smallest meaningful units)
                        > 
                        > ---
                        > 
                        > ## 🧩 Example
                        > 
                        > ```
                        > letresult=10+20;
                        > ```
                        > 
                        > ⬇️ Tokens:
                        > 
                        > ```
                        > [LET] [IDENTIFIER: result] [=] [NUMBER: 10] [+] [NUMBER: 20] [;]
                        > ```
                        > 
                        > ---
                        > 
                        > ## 💡 Key Idea
                        > 
                        > Tokenizer does **NOT** understand logic
                        > 
                        > It only understands:
                        > 
                        > - Keywords (`let`, `if`, `return`)
                        > - Identifiers (`result`)
                        > - Literals (`10`, `"hello"`)
                        > - Operators (`+`, `=`)
                        > 
                        > ---
                        > 
                        > ## ⚡ Important Insight (Senior Level)
                        > 
                        > 👉 Tokenizer is **stateful**
                        > 
                        > Example:
                        > 
                        > ```
                        > /abc/// regex
                        > a/b// division
                        > ```
                        > 
                        > Same `/`, different meaning → tokenizer decides based on context
                        > 
                    - Syntax Analysis (Parser)
                        
                        > 
                        > 
                        > 
                        > Now tokens → **structure**
                        > 
                        > ---
                        > 
                        > ## 🧠 What Parser Does
                        > 
                        > - Checks grammar (is code valid?)
                        > - Builds AST (Abstract Syntax Tree)
                        > 
                        > ---
                        > 
                        > ## ❌ Syntax Error Example
                        > 
                        > ```
                        > let=10;
                        > ```
                        > 
                        > 👉 Parser throws error
                        > 
                        > 👉 Execution stops here
                        > 
                        > ---
                        > 
                        > ## ✅ Valid Example → AST
                        > 
                        > ```
                        > letresult=10+20;
                        > ```
                        > 
                        > ---
                        > 
                        > ## 🌳 AST Representation
                        > 
                        > ```
                        > VariableDeclaration
                        >  ├── Identifier (result)
                        >  └── BinaryExpression (+)
                        >       ├── Literal (10)
                        >       └── Literal (20)
                        > ```
                        > 
                        > ---
                        > 
                        > ## 💡 Key Insight
                        > 
                        > 👉 AST = **true meaning of your code**
                        > 
                        > Everything later (optimization, execution) depends on this tree.
                        > 
                    - V8 Uses TWO Parsers (Important!)
                        - pre-parser
                            
                            > 
                            > 
                            > 
                            > ## 🥇 1. Pre-Parser (Fast & Lazy)
                            > 
                            > 👉 Used for performance
                            > 
                            > - Skips full parsing
                            > - Checks only structure roughly
                            > - Does NOT build full AST
                            > 
                            > ---
                            > 
                            > ### 🔥 Why?
                            > 
                            > Because JS can be huge:
                            > 
                            > ```
                            > functionbig() {
                            > // 10,000 lines
                            > }
                            > ```
                            > 
                            > 👉 If function is never called → waste of time parsing fully
                            > 
                        - Full Parser
                            
                            > 
                            > 
                            > 
                            > 👉 Runs only when needed
                            > 
                            > - Builds full AST
                            > - Used for execution
                            > 
                            > ---
                            > 
                            > ## 🧠 Lazy Parsing Concept
                            > 
                            > ```
                            > functionfoo() {
                            > return10+20;
                            > }
                            > ```
                            > 
                            > 👉 `foo` is NOT parsed fully until:
                            > 
                            > ```
                            > foo();
                            > ```
                            > 
                            > ---
                            > 
                            > ## 💡 This is HUGE for performance
                            > 
                            > - Faster startup 🚀
                            > - Less memory usage 🧠
                    - Scope Analysis (During Parsing)
                        
                        > 
                        > 
                        > 
                        > Parser also:
                        > 
                        > - Tracks variables
                        > - Builds scope chain
                        > 
                        > ---
                        > 
                        > ## Example
                        > 
                        > ```
                        > functiontest() {
                        > letx=10;
                        > }
                        > ```
                        > 
                        > Parser records:
                        > 
                        > - `x` belongs to `test` scope
                        > 
                        > ---
                        > 
                        > ## 🔥 Why Important?
                        > 
                        > Used later for:
                        > 
                        > - Closures
                        > - Memory allocation
                        > - Optimization
                    - Early Optimizations During Parsing
                        
                        > 
                        > 
                        > 
                        > Even at parsing stage, V8:
                        > 
                        > - Detects constant expressions
                        > - Marks functions for optimization
                        > 
                        > ---
                        > 
                        > ## Example
                        > 
                        > ```
                        > constx=10+20;
                        > ```
                        > 
                        > 👉 Can already simplify internally
                        > 
                    - Senior level insights
                        
                        > 
                        > 
                        > 
                        > ### 1. Parsing is NOT just syntax checking
                        > 
                        > It builds:
                        > 
                        > - AST
                        > - Scope info
                        > - Optimization hints
                        > 
                        > ---
                        > 
                        > ### 2. Lazy parsing = performance trick
                        > 
                        > - Functions parsed only when used
                        > 
                        > ---
                        > 
                        > ### 3. AST is EVERYTHING
                        > 
                        > If AST is bad → performance suffers later
                        > 
                        > ---
                        > 
                        > ### 4. Parser affects runtime speed
                        > 
                        > Bad patterns → harder to optimize later
                        > 
            - AST → Bytecode (Ignition Deep Dive)
                - DEFINITION
                - From AST to Bytecode
                    
                    > 
                    > 
                    > 
                    > Let’s take a simple example:
                    > 
                    > ```
                    > functionadd(a,b) {
                    > returna+b;
                    > }
                    > ```
                    > 
                    > ---
                    > 
                    > ## 🌳 AST (simplified)
                    > 
                    > ```
                    > FunctionDeclaration
                    >  ├── name: add
                    >  ├── params: a, b
                    >  └── body:
                    >       ReturnStatement
                    >         └── BinaryExpression (+)
                    > ```
                    > 
                    > ---
                    > 
                    > ## ⚡ Generated Bytecode (conceptual)
                    > 
                    > ```
                    > Ldar a        ; load a
                    > Add b         ; add b
                    > Return        ; return result
                    > ```
                    > 
                    > ---
                    > 
                    > ## 💡 Key Idea
                    > 
                    > 👉 AST = structure
                    > 👉 Bytecode = **instructions to execute that structure**
                    > 
                - Constant Folding (Micro Optimization)
                    
                    > 
                    > 
                    > 
                    > Ignition can optimize simple things:
                    > 
                    > ```
                    > constx=10+20;
                    > ```
                    > 
                    > 👉 Instead of computing at runtime:
                    > 
                    > ```
                    > LdaSmi 30
                    > Star r0
                    > ```
                    > 
                - INLINE CACHING
                    
                    > 
                    > 
                    > 
                    > While generating/executing bytecode:
                    > 
                    > 👉 V8 inserts **Inline Caches**
                    > 
                    > ---
                    > 
                    > ## Example
                    > 
                    > ```
                    > obj.x
                    > ```
                    > 
                    > First time:
                    > 
                    > - Unknown shape → slow lookup
                    > 
                    > After:
                    > 
                    > - Cached → fast lookup
                    > 
                    > ---
                    > 
                    > ## 💡 Why IC matters?
                    > 
                    > - Bridges interpreter → optimizer
                    > - Feeds data to TurboFan
                - Feedback Collection (Hidden Power)
                    
                    > 
                    > 
                    > 
                    > While running bytecode, V8 collects:
                    > 
                    > - Types of variables
                    > - Function call patterns
                    > - Object shapes
                    > 
                    > ---
                    > 
                    > ## Example
                    > 
                    > ```
                    > add(10,20)
                    > add(30,40)
                    > ```
                    > 
                    > 👉 V8 learns:
                    > 
                    > ```
                    > a = number
                    > b = number
                    > ```
                    > 
                    > ---
                    > 
                    > ## ⚡ This enables:
                    > 
                    > 👉 Future optimization (TurboFan)
                    > 
                - Dynamic Nature Handling
                    
                    > 
                    > 
                    > 
                    > JS allows:
                    > 
                    > ```
                    > add(10,20)
                    > add("a","b")
                    > ```
                    > 
                    > So bytecode must be:
                    > 
                    > - Flexible
                    > - Safe
                    > - Not over-optimized yet
                - Function Handling in Bytecode
                    
                    > 
                    > 
                    > 
                    > Functions are:
                    > 
                    > - Compiled into their own bytecode
                    > - Stored separately
                    > - Executed when called
                    > 
                    > ---
                    > 
                    > ## Lazy Compilation Again
                    > 
                    > ```
                    > functionbig() {
                    > // heavy code
                    > }
                    > ```
                    > 
                    > 👉 Bytecode generated only when:
                    > 
                    > ```
                    > big();
                    > ```
                    > 
                - Execution Loop (Interpreter)
                    
                    > 
                    > 
                    > 
                    > Ignition runs:
                    > 
                    > ```
                    > Read instruction → Execute → Next instruction
                    > ```
                    > 
                    > ---
                    > 
                    > ## Example Flow
                    > 
                    > ```
                    > LdaSmi 10
                    > AddSmi 20
                    > Star r0
                    > ```
                    > 
                    > Execution:
                    > 
                    > 1. Load 10
                    > 2. Add 20
                    > 3. Store result
                - FINAL FLOW (AST → Bytecode)
                    
                    > 
                    > 
                    > 
                    > AST
                    > ↓
                    > Ignition walks AST
                    > ↓
                    > Generate Bytecode
                    > ↓
                    > Execute Bytecode
                    > ↓
                    > Collect Feedback (types, usage)
                    > ↓
                    > Mark hot code
                    > 
                - 🎯 Senior-Level Insights
                    
                    > 
                    > 
                    > 
                    > ### 1. Ignition is NOT just interpreter
                    > 
                    > It also:
                    > 
                    > - Generates bytecode
                    > - Collects optimization data
                    > 
                    > ---
                    > 
                    > ### 2. Bytecode is temporary
                    > 
                    > - Will be replaced by optimized machine code later
                    > 
                    > ---
                    > 
                    > ### 3. Inline Caching is CRITICAL
                    > 
                    > 👉 Without it → no optimization
                    > 
                    > ---
                    > 
                    > ### 4. Register-based design = faster
                    > 
                    > 👉 Better than stack-based interpreters
                    > 
                    > ---
                    > 
                    > ### 5. This phase decides performance future
                    > 
                    > Bad patterns here → bad optimization later
                    > 
                    > ---
                    > 
                    > # 🚀 What You Should Do Next
                    > 
                    > Now you have 2 strong options:
                    > 
                    > ---
                    > 
                    > ## Option 1 (Recommended 🔥)
                    > 
                    > 👉 **TurboFan (Optimization Phase)**
                    > 
                    > Understand:
                    > 
                    > - JIT compilation
                    > - Hot code optimization
                    > - Deoptimization
                    > 
                    > ---
                    > 
                    > ## Option 2 (Deep Internals)
                    > 
                    > 👉 **Hidden Classes + Inline Caching (VERY IMPORTANT)**
                    > 
                    > This is what separates mid vs senior devs.
                    > 
            - Execution Phase (Interpreter Running — Ignition)
                - High-Level Flow
                    
                    > 
                    > 
                    > 
                    > This phase happens inside the V8 JavaScript Engine using:
                    > 
                    > 👉 **Ignition (the interpreter)**
                    > 
                    > ---
                    > 
                    > # 🚀 High-Level Flow
                    > 
                    > ```
                    > Bytecode → Interpreter Loop → Execution → Feedback Collection
                    > ```
                    > 
                    > ---
                    > 
                    > # 🧠 1. What “Execution” Really Means
                    > 
                    > At this point you have:
                    > 
                    > - Bytecode ✅
                    > - Registers ✅
                    > - Execution context ✅
                    > 
                    > 👉 Now V8 starts a loop:
                    > 
                    > ```
                    > Fetch → Decode → Execute → Repeat
                    > ```
                    > 
                - The Interpreter Loop (Core Mechanism)
                    
                    > 
                    > 
                    > 
                    > Ignition runs something like:
                    > 
                    > ```
                    > while (true) {
                    >   instruction = next();
                    >   execute(instruction);
                    > }
                    > ```
                    > 
                    > ---
                    > 
                    > ## ⚡ Example Bytecode
                    > 
                    > ```
                    > LdaSmi 10
                    > AddSmi 20
                    > Star r0
                    > ```
                    > 
                    > ---
                    > 
                    > ## 🧩 Step-by-Step Execution
                    > 
                    > ### 1️⃣ `LdaSmi 10`
                    > 
                    > 👉 Load integer `10` into accumulator
                    > 
                    > ---
                    > 
                    > ### 2️⃣ `AddSmi 20`
                    > 
                    > 👉 Add `20` to accumulator → result = `30`
                    > 
                    > ---
                    > 
                    > ### 3️⃣ `Star r0`
                    > 
                    > 👉 Store result in register `r0`
                    > 
                    > ---
                    > 
                    > ## 💡 Key Insight
                    > 
                    > 👉 Execution is **instruction-by-instruction**, not whole-program
                    > 
                - Execution Context & Call Stack
                    
                    > 
                    > 
                    > 
                    > Every time code runs, V8 creates:
                    > 
                    > 👉 **Execution Context**
                    > 
                    > ---
                    > 
                    > ## Example
                    > 
                    > ```
                    > functionadd(a,b) {
                    > returna+b;
                    > }
                    > 
                    > add(10,20);
                    > ```
                    > 
                    > ---
                    > 
                    > ## 🧩 What happens:
                    > 
                    > 1. Global context created
                    > 2. `add()` called → new context pushed
                    > 3. Executes inside that context
                    > 4. Returns → context popped
                    > 
                    > ---
                    > 
                    > ## 🔥 Call Stack
                    > 
                    > ```
                    > Global()
                    >   ↓
                    > add()
                    > ```
                    > 
                    > ---
                    > 
                    > ## 💡 Important
                    > 
                    > 👉 Stack = function calls
                    > 
                    > 👉 Heap = objects
                    > 
                - Registers & Accumulator
                    
                    > 
                    > 
                    > 
                    > Ignition uses:
                    > 
                    > - **Accumulator** (main working register)
                    > - **Registers** (`r0`, `r1`, …)
                    > 
                    > ---
                    > 
                    > ## Example
                    > 
                    > ```
                    > letx=10+20;
                    > ```
                    > 
                    > ---
                    > 
                    > Execution:
                    > 
                    > ```
                    > Accumulator = 10
                    > Accumulator = 10 + 20 → 30
                    > r0 = 30
                    > ```
                    > 
                    > ---
                    > 
                    > ## 💡 Why this matters
                    > 
                    > 👉 Faster than stack-based execution
                    > 
                    > 👉 Fewer memory operations
                    > 
                - Inline Caching (Happens During Execution)
                    
                    > 
                    > 
                    > 
                    > This is where things get **VERY interesting**.
                    > 
                    > ---
                    > 
                    > ## Example
                    > 
                    > ```
                    > user.name
                    > ```
                    > 
                    > ---
                    > 
                    > ### First time:
                    > 
                    > - V8 doesn’t know object structure
                    > - Does slow lookup
                    > 
                    > ---
                    > 
                    > ### After few runs:
                    > 
                    > - V8 caches location of `name`
                    > 
                    > ---
                    > 
                    > 👉 Next time:
                    > 
                    > ```
                    > Direct memory access (FAST)
                    > ```
                    > 
                    > ---
                    > 
                    > ## 🧠 Types of IC
                    > 
                    > - Monomorphic (1 type) ✅ fastest
                    > - Polymorphic (few types)
                    > - Megamorphic (many types) ❌ slow
                - Feedback Collection (Hidden Power)
                    
                    > 
                    > 
                    > 
                    > During execution, V8 collects:
                    > 
                    > - Variable types
                    > - Function usage
                    > - Object shapes
                    > 
                    > ---
                    > 
                    > ## Example
                    > 
                    > ```
                    > functionadd(a,b) {
                    > returna+b;
                    > }
                    > 
                    > add(1,2);
                    > add(3,4);
                    > ```
                    > 
                    > ---
                    > 
                    > 👉 V8 records:
                    > 
                    > ```
                    > a = number
                    > b = number
                    > ```
                    > 
                    > ---
                    > 
                    > ## ⚡ Why?
                    > 
                    > 👉 This data is sent to **TurboFan later**
                    > 
                - Handling Dynamic JavaScript
                    
                    > 
                    > 
                    > 
                    > JS can change types anytime:
                    > 
                    > ```
                    > add(1,2)
                    > add("a","b")
                    > ```
                    > 
                    > ---
                    > 
                    > 👉 So Ignition:
                    > 
                    > - Stays flexible
                    > - Avoids heavy optimization
                    > - Keeps execution safe
                - Hot Code Detection
                    
                    > 
                    > 
                    > 
                    > V8 tracks:
                    > 
                    > 👉 Which code runs frequently
                    > 
                    > ---
                    > 
                    > ## Example
                    > 
                    > ```
                    > for (leti=0;i<100000;i++) {
                    > add(i,i);
                    > }
                    > ```
                    > 
                    > ---
                    > 
                    > 👉 `add()` becomes:
                    > 
                    > ```
                    > HOT FUNCTION 🔥
                    > ```
                    > 
                    > ---
                    > 
                    > ## 💡 What happens next?
                    > 
                    > 👉 Sent to **TurboFan (optimizer)**
                    > 
                - Memory Interaction During Execution
                    
                    > 
                    > 
                    > 
                    > Execution also:
                    > 
                    > - Allocates objects in heap
                    > - Uses stack for function calls
                    > 
                    > ---
                    > 
                    > ## Example
                    > 
                    > ```
                    > letobj= { x:10 };
                    > ```
                    > 
                    > ---
                    > 
                    > 👉 Happens:
                    > 
                    > - Object → heap
                    > - Reference → stack
                - Interaction with Runtime (Event Loop)
                    
                    > 
                    > 
                    > 
                    > Important:
                    > 
                    > 👉 V8 executes **synchronous code only**
                    > 
                    > Async handled by:
                    > 
                    > 👉 Node.js or browser
                    > 
                    > ---
                    > 
                    > ## Flow
                    > 
                    > ```
                    > Call Stack → Web APIs → Callback Queue → Event Loop → Back to V8
                    > ```
                    > 
                    > ---
                    > 
                    > # 🔥 FINAL FLOW (Execution Phase)
                    > 
                    > ```
                    > Bytecode
                    >   ↓
                    > Ignition Interpreter Loop
                    >   ↓
                    > Execute Instructions (line-by-line)
                    >   ↓
                    > Manage Call Stack & Contexts
                    >   ↓
                    > Use Registers & Accumulator
                    >   ↓
                    > Inline Caching (optimize access)
                    >   ↓
                    > Collect Feedback (types, patterns)
                    >   ↓
                    > Detect Hot Code 🔥
                    > ```
                    > 
                - Senior-Level Insights (CRITICAL)
                    
                    > 
                    > 
                    > 
                    > # 🎯 Senior-Level Insights (CRITICAL)
                    > 
                    > ### 1. Execution is NOT just running code
                    > 
                    > It also:
                    > 
                    > - Learns patterns
                    > - Prepares optimization
                    > 
                    > ---
                    > 
                    > ### 2. Inline Caching = performance backbone
                    > 
                    > 👉 Without IC → JS would be slow
                    > 
                    > ---
                    > 
                    > ### 3. Hot code detection drives JIT
                    > 
                    > 👉 Execution phase decides what gets optimized
                    > 
                    > ---
                    > 
                    > ### 4. Clean code = better optimization
                    > 
                    > Bad:
                    > 
                    > ```
                    > obj.x
                    > obj["x"]
                    > obj[randomKey]
                    > ```
                    > 
                    > 👉 Causes megamorphic IC → slow
                    > 
                    > ---
                    > 
                    > ### 5. Stable types = faster JS
                    > 
                    > Good:
                    > 
                    > ```
                    > add(1,2)
                    > add(3,4)
                    > ```
                    > 
                    > Bad:
                    > 
                    > ```
                    > add(1,2)
                    > add("a","b")
                    > ```
                    > 
                    > ---
                    > 
                    > # 🚀 Next Step (Very Important)
                    > 
                    > Now comes the most powerful part:
                    > 
                    > 👉 **TurboFan (JIT Optimization Phase)**
                    > 
                    > This is where JS becomes:
                    > 
                    > ⚡ Near C++ speed
                    > 
            - Profiling & Optimization Trigger (V8 Deep Dive)
                - DEFINITION
                    
                    > 
                    > 
                    > 
                    > Inside the V8 JavaScript Engine, this phase runs **during execution** (not after).
                    > 
                    > 👉 It continuously observes your code.
                    > 
                    > ---
                    > 
                    > # 🚀 High-Level Flow
                    > 
                    > ```
                    > Execution → Profiling → Hot Code Detection → Optimization Trigger
                    > ```
                    > 
                    > ---
                    > 
                    > # 🔍 1. What is Profiling?
                    > 
                    > 👉 Profiling = **collecting runtime data about your code**
                    > 
                    > Not static analysis ❌
                    > 
                    > Not compile-time ❌
                    > 
                    > 👉 It happens **while your program runs**
                    > 
                - STEPS
                    - What V8 Tracks
                        
                        > 
                        > 
                        > 
                        > ### 1. Function frequency
                        > 
                        > ```
                        > functionadd(a,b) {
                        > returna+b;
                        > }
                        > ```
                        > 
                        > If called many times → important
                        > 
                        > ---
                        > 
                        > ### 2. Variable types
                        > 
                        > ```
                        > add(10,20)
                        > add(30,40)
                        > ```
                        > 
                        > 👉 V8 records:
                        > 
                        > ```
                        > a → number
                        > b → number
                        > ```
                        > 
                        > ---
                        > 
                        > ### 3. Object shapes (Hidden Classes)
                        > 
                        > ```
                        > user.name
                        > ```
                        > 
                        > 👉 Tracks structure of `user`
                        > 
                        > ---
                        > 
                        > ### 4. Property access patterns
                        > 
                        > ```
                        > obj.x
                        > obj.x
                        > obj.x
                        > ```
                        > 
                        > 👉 Repeated → cacheable
                        > 
                    - Inline Caches = Data Source
                        
                        > 
                        > 
                        > 
                        > Profiling relies heavily on:
                        > 
                        > 👉 **Inline Caches (ICs)**
                        > 
                        > ---
                        > 
                        > ## Example
                        > 
                        > ```
                        > user.name
                        > ```
                        > 
                        > ---
                        > 
                        > ### First run:
                        > 
                        > - Slow lookup
                        > - Cache created
                        > 
                        > ---
                        > 
                        > ### Later runs:
                        > 
                        > - IC stores:
                        > 
                        > ```
                        > "object shape → property location"
                        > ```
                        > 
                        > ---
                        > 
                        > ## 🧠 IC States
                        > 
                        > | State | Meaning |
                        > | --- | --- |
                        > | Monomorphic | 1 type → ✅ fastest |
                        > | Polymorphic | few types |
                        > | Megamorphic | many types → ❌ slow |
                        > 
                        > ---
                        > 
                        > ## 💡 Critical Insight
                        > 
                        > 👉 ICs are the **main input to the optimizer**
                        > 
                    - Hot Code Detection
                        
                        > 
                        > 
                        > 
                        > V8 identifies:
                        > 
                        > 👉 **HOT code = frequently executed code**
                        > 
                        > ---
                        > 
                        > ## Example
                        > 
                        > ```
                        > for (leti=0;i<100000;i++) {
                        > add(i,i);
                        > }
                        > ```
                        > 
                        > ---
                        > 
                        > 👉 `add()` becomes:
                        > 
                        > ```
                        > 🔥 HOT FUNCTION
                        > ```
                        > 
                        > ---
                        > 
                        > ## 🧠 How V8 decides?
                        > 
                        > Uses:
                        > 
                        > - Execution counters
                        > - Call frequency
                        > - Loop iterations
                        > 
                        > ---
                        > 
                        > ## ⚡ Threshold Concept
                        > 
                        > 👉 Not officially fixed, but:
                        > 
                        > ```
                        > If function runs “enough times” → optimize it
                        > ```
                        > 
                    - Optimization Trigger
                        
                        > 
                        > 
                        > 
                        > Once code is HOT:
                        > 
                        > 👉 V8 sends it to:
                        > 
                        > ➡️ **TurboFan (Optimizing Compiler)**
                        > 
                        > ---
                        > 
                        > ## Flow
                        > 
                        > ```
                        > Bytecode (Ignition)
                        >    ↓
                        > Profiling Data
                        >    ↓
                        > HOT Function Detected 🔥
                        >    ↓
                        > Send to TurboFan
                        > ```
                        > 
                    - What Makes Code Optimizable?
                        
                        > 
                        > 
                        > 
                        > V8 checks if code is:
                        > 
                        > ---
                        > 
                        > ## ✅ Good for Optimization
                        > 
                        > ### Stable types
                        > 
                        > ```
                        > add(1,2)
                        > add(3,4)
                        > ```
                        > 
                        > ---
                        > 
                        > ### Predictable objects
                        > 
                        > ```
                        > user= { name:"Ali", age:20 }
                        > ```
                        > 
                        > ---
                        > 
                        > ### Consistent property access
                        > 
                        > ```
                        > user.name
                        > ```
                        > 
                        > ---
                        > 
                        > ---
                        > 
                        > ## ❌ Bad for Optimization
                        > 
                        > ### Changing types
                        > 
                        > ```
                        > add(1,2)
                        > add("a","b")
                        > ```
                        > 
                        > ---
                        > 
                        > ### Dynamic object structure
                        > 
                        > ```
                        > obj.x=10
                        > obj.y=20
                        > deleteobj.x
                        > ```
                        > 
                        > ---
                        > 
                        > ### Random property access
                        > 
                        > ```
                        > obj[randomKey]
                        > ```
                        > 
                        > ---
                        > 
                        > ## 💡 Insight
                        > 
                        > 👉 V8 optimizes **predictability**, not complexity
                        > 
                    - Optimization is Speculative
                        
                        > 
                        > 
                        > 
                        > This is VERY IMPORTANT.
                        > 
                        > 👉 V8 assumes things based on profiling
                        > 
                        > ---
                        > 
                        > ## Example
                        > 
                        > ```
                        > add(1,2)
                        > add(3,4)
                        > ```
                        > 
                        > 👉 Assumption:
                        > 
                        > ```
                        > a, b are always numbers
                        > ```
                        > 
                        > ---
                        > 
                        > ## But later:
                        > 
                        > ```
                        > add("a","b")
                        > ```
                        > 
                        > 💥 Assumption breaks
                        > 
                        > ---
                        > 
                        > 👉 Leads to:
                        > 
                        > ```
                        > DEOPTIMIZATION
                        > ```
                        > 
                        > (back to slow mode)
                        > 
                    - Tiered Execution Model
                        
                        > 
                        > 
                        > 
                        > V8 uses:
                        > 
                        > ---
                        > 
                        > ## 🥉 Tier 1 — Ignition
                        > 
                        > - Interpreter
                        > - Slow but flexible
                        > 
                        > ---
                        > 
                        > ## 🥇 Tier 2 — TurboFan
                        > 
                        > - Optimized machine code
                        > - Fast but strict
                        > 
                        > ---
                        > 
                        > ## Flow
                        > 
                        > ```
                        > Ignition → Profiling → TurboFan → (maybe Deopt)
                        > ```
                        > 
                    - Continuous Feedback Loop
                        
                        > 
                        > 
                        > 
                        > This is NOT one-time.
                        > 
                        > ```
                        > Execute → Profile → Optimize → Deopt → Re-optimize
                        > ```
                        > 
                        > ---
                        > 
                        > 👉 V8 constantly adapts
                        > 
                        > ---
                        > 
                        > # 🔥 FINAL FLOW (Profiling Phase)
                        > 
                        > ```
                        > Bytecode Execution (Ignition)
                        >    ↓
                        > Inline Caches collect data
                        >    ↓
                        > Profiler tracks:
                        >    - Function calls
                        >    - Types
                        >    - Object shapes
                        >    ↓
                        > Hot Code Detected 🔥
                        >    ↓
                        > Optimization Trigger
                        >    ↓
                        > Send to TurboFan
                        > ```
                        > 
                    - FINAL
                        
                        > 
                        > 
                        > 
                        > # 🎯 Senior-Level Insights (CRITICAL)
                        > 
                        > ### 1. JS performance = predictability
                        > 
                        > 👉 Not about fewer lines, but consistent behavior
                        > 
                        > ---
                        > 
                        > ### 2. Inline Caches drive everything
                        > 
                        > 👉 IC → Profiling → Optimization
                        > 
                        > ---
                        > 
                        > ### 3. Optimization is temporary
                        > 
                        > 👉 Can break anytime → deopt
                        > 
                        > ---
                        > 
                        > ### 4. Hot code matters most
                        > 
                        > 👉 Only frequently used code gets optimized
                        > 
                        > ---
                        > 
                        > ### 5. You don’t optimize JS — you guide V8
                        > 
                        > Bad:
                        > 
                        > ```
                        > obj[key]
                        > ```
                        > 
                        > Good:
                        > 
                        > ```
                        > obj.name
                        > ```
                        > 
                        > ---
                        > 
                        > # 🚀 Next Step (MOST IMPORTANT PART 🔥)
                        > 
                        > Now comes the **heart of performance**:
                        > 
                        > 👉 **TurboFan (Optimizing Compiler)**
                        > 
                        > This is where:
                        > 
                        > ⚡ JS → optimized machine code
                        > 
                        > ⚡ JIT compilation happens
                        > 
                        > ---
                        > 
                        > Or go deeper into internals:
                        > 
                        > 👉 Hidden Classes + Inline Caching (advanced mastery)
                        > 
            - TurboFan Optimization (JIT Compiler Deep Dive)
                - DEFINITION
                    
                    > 
                    > 
                    > 
                    > Inside the V8 JavaScript Engine, **TurboFan** is the:
                    > 
                    > 👉 **Optimizing Just-In-Time (JIT) compiler**
                    > 
                    > ---
                    > 
                    > # ⚡ High-Level Flow
                    > 
                    > ```
                    > Hot Code 🔥 → TurboFan → Optimized Machine Code → Fast Execution
                    > ```
                    > 
                    > ---
                    > 
                    > # 🧠 1. Why TurboFan Exists
                    > 
                    > Ignition (interpreter):
                    > 
                    > - Fast startup ✅
                    > - Flexible ✅
                    > - Slow execution ❌
                    > 
                    > ---
                    > 
                    > 👉 TurboFan solves:
                    > 
                    > ```
                    > Make frequently used code run at near C++ speed ⚡
                    > ```
                    > 
                - Input to TurboFan
                    
                    > 
                    > 
                    > 
                    > TurboFan does NOT start from scratch.
                    > 
                    > It receives:
                    > 
                    > - Bytecode (from Ignition)
                    > - Profiling data (VERY IMPORTANT)
                    > 
                    > ---
                    > 
                    > ## 🧩 Example
                    > 
                    > ```
                    > functionadd(a,b) {
                    > returna+b;
                    > }
                    > 
                    > add(10,20);
                    > add(30,40);
                    > ```
                    > 
                    > ---
                    > 
                    > ### Profiling says:
                    > 
                    > ```
                    > a → number
                    > b → number
                    > ```
                    > 
                    > ---
                    > 
                    > 👉 TurboFan uses this to specialize code
                    > 
                - TurboFan Compilation Pipeline
                    - STEP 1
                        
                        > 
                        > 
                        > 
                        > This is where things get **serious (senior level)**.
                        > 
                        > ---
                        > 
                        > ## 🧠 Step 1: Build Intermediate Representation (IR)
                        > 
                        > TurboFan converts bytecode → **IR graph**
                        > 
                        > 👉 Think:
                        > 
                        > ```
                        > Graph of operations (nodes + edges)
                        > ```
                        > 
                        > ---
                        > 
                        > ## Example (conceptual)
                        > 
                        > ```
                        > a ----\
                        >        (+) ----> return
                        > b ----/
                        > ```
                        > 
                        > ---
                        > 
                        > ## 💡 Why graph?
                        > 
                        > 👉 Easier to optimize than linear code
                        > 
                        
                    - STEP 2
                        
                        > 
                        > 
                        > 
                        > # ⚡ Step 2: Optimization Passes
                        > 
                        > TurboFan applies MANY optimizations:
                        > 
                        > ---
                        > 
                        > ## 🔥 1. Inlining
                        > 
                        > ```
                        > functionadd(a,b) {
                        > returna+b;
                        > }
                        > 
                        > functioncalc() {
                        > returnadd(1,2);
                        > }
                        > ```
                        > 
                        > ---
                        > 
                        > 👉 Becomes:
                        > 
                        > ```
                        > functioncalc() {
                        > return1+2;
                        > ```
                        > 
                        - Type Specialization
                            
                            > 
                            > 
                            > 
                            > Since:
                            > 
                            > ```
                            > a, b = number
                            > ```
                            > 
                            > ---
                            > 
                            > 👉 Removes type checks:
                            > 
                            > ❌ Before:
                            > 
                            > ```
                            > Check type → then add
                            > ```
                            > 
                            > ✅ After:
                            > 
                            > ```
                            > Direct integer addition
                            > ```
                            > 
                        - Constant Folding
                            
                            > 
                            > 
                            > 
                            > ```
                            > constx=10+20;
                            > ```
                            > 
                            > 👉 Becomes:
                            > 
                            > ```
                            > constx=30;
                            > ```
                            > 
                        - Dead Code Elimination
                            
                            > 
                            > 
                            > 
                            > ```
                            > if (false) {
                            > doSomething();
                            > }
                            > ```
                            > 
                            > 👉 Removed completely
                            > 
                        - Hidden Class Optimization
                            
                            > 
                            > 
                            > 
                            > Objects with same structure:
                            > 
                            > ```
                            > {name:"Ali",age:20 }
                            > ```
                            > 
                            > 👉 Optimized as:
                            > 
                            > ```
                            > Fixed memory layout
                            > ```
                            > 
                    - STEP 3
                        - Generate Machine Code
                            - DEFINITION
                                
                                > 
                                > 
                                > 
                                > After optimization:
                                > 
                                > 👉 TurboFan generates:
                                > 
                                > ```
                                > REAL CPU instructions (x86 / ARM)
                                > ```
                                > 
                                > ---
                                > 
                                > ## 💡 Important
                                > 
                                > 👉 This is NOT bytecode anymore
                                > 
                                > 👉 This runs directly on CPU
                                > 
                            - Optimized Execution
                                
                                > 
                                > 
                                > 
                                > Now your function runs:
                                > 
                                > - No interpreter ❌
                                > - No type checks ❌ (mostly)
                                > - Direct memory access ✅
                                > 
                                > ---
                                > 
                                > ## 🚀 Result
                                > 
                                > ```
                                > ⚡ 10x–100x faster execution
                                > ```
                                > 
                                > (depending on code)
                                > 
                            - Speculative Optimization (CRITICAL)
                                
                                > 
                                > 
                                > 
                                > TurboFan assumes:
                                > 
                                > 👉 “Your code will behave the same”
                                > 
                                > ---
                                > 
                                > ## Example
                                > 
                                > ```
                                > add(10,20);
                                > add(30,40);
                                > ```
                                > 
                                > Assumption:
                                > 
                                > ```
                                > numbers only
                                > ```
                                > 
                                > ---
                                > 
                                > ## ❌ If broken:
                                > 
                                > ```
                                > add("a","b");
                                > ```
                                > 
                                > 💥 Problem:
                                > 
                                > - Optimized code is now invalid
                                > 
                                > ---
                                > 
                                > 👉 V8 triggers:
                                > 
                                > ```
                                > DEOPTIMIZATION
                                > ```
                                > 
                                > (back to Ignition)
                                > 
                            - Deoptimization Flow
                                
                                > 
                                > 
                                > 
                                > Optimized Code
                                > 
                                > ↓
                                > 
                                > Wrong assumption ❌
                                > 
                                > ↓
                                > 
                                > Deopt triggered 💥
                                > 
                                > ↓
                                > 
                                > Fallback to Bytecode (Ignition)
                                > 
                                > ↓
                                > 
                                > Re-profile → Re-optimize
                                > 
                            - On-Stack Replacement (OSR)
                                
                                > 
                                > 
                                > 
                                > Advanced concept
                                > 
                                > ---
                                > 
                                > ## What is it?
                                > 
                                > 👉 Switching from interpreter → optimized code
                                > 
                                > **while the function is still running**
                                > 
                                > ---
                                > 
                                > ## Example
                                > 
                                > ```
                                > for (leti=0;i<1_000_000;i++) {
                                > sum+=i;
                                > }
                                > ```
                                > 
                                > ---
                                > 
                                > 👉 Mid-loop:
                                > 
                                > ```
                                > Ignition → TurboFan (switch happens here)
                                > ```
                                > 
                                > ---
                                > 
                                > ## 💡 Result
                                > 
                                > - Loop starts slow
                                > - Becomes fast mid-execution
                            - Bailouts (Safety Mechanism)
                                
                                > 
                                > 
                                > 
                                > If something unexpected happens:
                                > 
                                > 👉 TurboFan inserts **bailout points**
                                > 
                                > ---
                                > 
                                > ## Example
                                > 
                                > ```
                                > obj.x
                                > ```
                                > 
                                > If shape changes:
                                > 
                                > 👉 bailout → deopt
                                > 
                                > ---
                                > 
                                > # 🔥 FINAL FLOW (TurboFan)
                                > 
                                > ```
                                > Hot Function 🔥
                                >    ↓
                                > Send to TurboFan
                                >    ↓
                                > Build IR Graph
                                >    ↓
                                > Apply Optimizations:
                                >    - Inlining
                                >    - Type specialization
                                >    - Constant folding
                                >    - Dead code removal
                                >    ↓
                                > Generate Machine Code
                                >    ↓
                                > Execute FAST ⚡
                                >    ↓
                                > (If assumption breaks → Deopt 💥)
                                > ```
                                > 
                            - 
                    - Senior-Level Insights (VERY IMPORTANT)
                        
                        > 
                        > 
                        > 
                        > ### 1. TurboFan is speculative
                        > 
                        > 👉 It bets on your code being predictable
                        > 
                        > ---
                        > 
                        > ### 2. Stability = performance
                        > 
                        > Good:
                        > 
                        > ```
                        > obj.name
                        > obj.name
                        > obj.name
                        > ```
                        > 
                        > Bad:
                        > 
                        > ```
                        > obj[randomKey]
                        > ```
                        > 
                        > ---
                        > 
                        > ### 3. Types matter A LOT
                        > 
                        > Stable:
                        > 
                        > ```
                        > add(1,2)
                        > ```
                        > 
                        > Unstable:
                        > 
                        > ```
                        > add(1,"2")
                        > ```
                        > 
                        > ---
                        > 
                        > ### 4. Hidden classes are critical
                        > 
                        > 👉 Same object structure → huge speed boost
                        > 
                        > ---
                        > 
                        > ### 5. Deopt kills performance
                        > 
                        > 👉 Avoid unpredictable behavior
                        > 
                        > ---
